question: Why is the power-holder called stainless if will, knowledge, and action appear separately?
premises: Will, knowledge, and action appear as distinct.
The power-holder may seem affected by these distinctions.
Power itself is never truly affected by anything.
inference: The apparent separate affection of will, knowledge, and action does not stain the power-holder, because power is never truly affected.
uncertainties: The syntax contrasts apparent affection with ultimate unaffectedness.
plain_english: The power-holder seems affected because will, knowledge, and action appear separately; yet power itself is never affected by anything.
